ai.literal: Without doing, to the help done, earth and heaven and equaling is difficult.
ai.translation: For a help done without any prior favor, giving the earth and the heavens is hardly an equal return.
ai.modern: நாம் முன்பு எந்த உதவியும் செய்யாமல் இருக்கும்போது, நமக்கு ஒருவன் செய்த உதவிக்கு, இந்த உலகத்தையும் வானுலகத்தையும் கைமாறாகக் கொடுத்தாலும் அது ஈடாகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immense value of unprompted, spontaneous help. The phrase 'ceyyāmal ceyta' refers to assistance given without the receiver having done any prior favor to the giver. To compensate for such pure generosity, the poet states that even offering the entire earth and the heavens would not be an equal return. It teaches that true gratitude recognizes the incomparable worth of unsolicited kindness.

ai.literal: At the appropriate time done help, small even if, than the world greatly greater.
ai.translation: A good deed done at the right time, even if small in measure, is vastly greater than the world.
ai.modern: தக்க காலத்தில் செய்யப்பட்ட உதவி சிறியதாக இருந்தாலும், அது இந்த உலகத்தை விட மிகப் பெரியதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense value of timely help. The word 'காலத்தினால்' shows that the worth of a good deed is measured not by its physical size, but by the critical need of the moment. Therefore, even a small act of assistance rendered exactly when needed is considered far greater than the earth itself.

ai.literal: Benefit weighing-not-they done help, excellence if-weighed, goodness sea-than is-greater.
ai.translation: If one weighs the excellence of a help done by those who did not weigh the return benefit, its goodness is greater than the sea.
ai.modern: தமக்கு என்ன பயன் கிடைக்கும் என்று ஆராயாமல் ஒருவர் செய்த உதவியின் சிறப்பை ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், அதன் நன்மை கடலை விடப் பெரியதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense value of selfless help. The phrase 'பயன் தூக்கார்' refers to people who do not calculate the return benefit before helping. When someone evaluates the true excellence ('நயன்') of such unselfish assistance, they will find its inherent goodness ('நன்மை') to be vast. The poet uses the sea ('கடலின் பெரிது') as a metaphor to show that such pure generosity is boundless and greater than the ocean itself.

ai.translation: Even if a good deed is as tiny as a millet seed, those who know its true value will consider it as large as a palmyra tree.

ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the tiny millet seed with the massive palmyra tree to illustrate how gratitude is measured. Even if a good deed is objectively small, its worth is not judged merely by its physical size. Those who truly understand the value of the help received will magnify it in their hearts, seeing it as vast as a palmyra tree.

ai.translation: The value of a help is not measured by the extent of the help itself. It is measured by the nobility of those who received it.
ai.modern: ஒருவருக்குச் செய்யும் உதவியின் மதிப்பு, அந்த உதவியின் அளவைப் பொறுத்தது அன்று. அது அந்த உதவியைப் பெற்றவர்களின் நற்பண்பின் அளவைப் பொறுத்தது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to measure the true worth of a good deed. The word 'உதவி' (help) is repeated to contrast the physical act of helping with its ultimate value. The extent ('வரைத்து') of a benefit is not determined by the material size of the help given. Instead, its true measure corresponds to the 'சால்பு' (nobility or worthiness) of the person who receives it, as a noble person will value even a small help immensely.

ai.literal: Do not forget blemish-without-they friendship; do not forsake sorrow-in support became-they friendship.
ai.translation: Do not forget the friendship of the flawless. Do not forsake the friendship of those who were your support in times of sorrow.
ai.modern: குற்றமற்றவர்களின் உறவை மறக்கக் கூடாது. துன்பம் வந்த காலத்தில் துணையாக இருந்தவர்களின் நட்பைக் கைவிடக் கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the lasting value of pure relationships and timely help. The word 'மாசற்றார்' refers to people of flawless character, whose friendship should always be cherished in one's memory. 'துப்பு' means strength or support, highlighting how true friends act as a pillar during times of affliction ('துன்பத்துள்'). By placing 'மறவற்க' (do not forget) and 'துறவற்க' (do not forsake) in parallel, the verse teaches that gratitude requires both remembering the good and never abandoning those who stood by us.

ai.literal: Seven-fold, in all seven births they will remember, their-upon distress wiped-away-those-who friendship.
ai.translation: Through all seven states of seven births, they will remember the friendship of those who wiped away their distress.
ai.modern: தமக்கு வந்த துன்பத்தைப் போக்கியவர்களின் நட்பை, நல்லோர் ஏழேழு பிறவிகளிலும் மறக்காமல் நினைப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the enduring nature of gratitude for true friendship. The phrase 'எழுமை எழுபிறப்பும்' (seven-fold seven births) is a classical Tamil idiom expressing eternity or a vast span of time, indicating that true gratitude transcends a single lifetime. 'விழுமம்' refers to deep distress or suffering, and 'துடைத்தவர்' evokes the physical act of wiping away tears or removing pain. Thus, the friendship of someone who rescues another from severe hardship is so profound that it will be cherished forever.

ai.literal: Good deed forgetting good is not; good that which is not that very day forgetting is good.
ai.translation: It is not good to forget a good deed. It is good to forget a bad deed that very day.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் செய்த நன்மையை மறப்பது நல்லதல்ல; அவர் செய்த தீமையை நடந்த அன்றே மறந்துவிடுவது நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts how one should handle good and bad deeds done by others. The word 'நன்றி' refers to a benefit or help received, which should never be forgotten. Conversely, 'நன்று அல்லது' (that which is not good) refers to a wrong or injury suffered. The couplet advises that while gratitude must be permanent, any resentment for a bad deed should be discarded 'அன்றே' (on that very day) to maintain one's own peace and virtue.

ai.literal: Killing-like harm even if [they] do, they did one good thing to think [of], [the harm] will perish.
ai.translation: Even if someone does you a harm as grievous as murder, it will vanish from your mind when you remember a single good thing they have done for you.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் நம்மைக் கொல்வது போன்ற பெருந்துன்பத்தைச் செய்தாலும், அவர் முன்பு செய்த ஒரு நன்மையை நினைத்துப் பார்த்தால் அந்தத் துன்பம் மறைந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of gratitude to overcome resentment. The phrase 'கொன்றன்ன இன்னா' (harm like killing) sets up the extreme case of someone causing the worst possible pain. Yet, the poet says that even if they commit such an act, the pain 'கெடும்' (will perish or be erased). The condition for this erasure is simply 'உள்ள' (to remember) just 'ஒன்று நன்று' (one good thing) that the same person did in the past. By focusing on a single past kindness, the mind lets go of even the most severe present injury.

ai.literal: Whatever good deed / to those who destroyed even / escape / there is / escape / is not / done good deed / who destroyed / to the person
ai.translation: There is redemption for those who have destroyed any other virtue, but there is no redemption for one who destroys the memory of a good deed done to them.
ai.modern: எந்த அறத்தை அழித்தவர்க்கும் தப்பிப் பிழைக்க ஒரு வழி இருக்கும். ஆனால், ஒருவர் செய்த உதவியை மறந்து அழித்தவனுக்குத் தப்பிப் பிழைக்க வழியே இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the destruction of general virtues with the destruction of gratitude. The word 'கொன்ற' (killed/destroyed) is used metaphorically to mean ruining or completely forgetting a virtue or a good deed. While a person might find a way to redeem themselves after committing other wrongs, the text asserts that there is absolutely no salvation for someone who is ungrateful for the help they have received.
